about: Vishal Nirmiti is a civil engineering and manufacturing company that makes pre-stressed concrete (PSC) railway sleepers and precast products, and fabricates large-diameter mild steel pipes, liners and penstock pipes for pumped storage projects. It also does job-work, runs a 1.8 MW windmill portfolio and leases property. It operates units across Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh and other states, with FY26 revenue of about 339 crore rupees.
sector: Railway infrastructure / PSC sleepers, MS pipes and civil construction
headquarters: Mumbai (registered office); corporate office in Pune, Maharashtra

objects.purpose: General corporate purposes (capped at 25% of fresh issue)

promoters.background: Tapadiya family-run business with 20+ years in railway sleepers; promoters hold 37.51% and promoter group 35.91% (73.42% combined) pre-offer. Selling shareholder Vaman Prestressing Company Pvt Ltd (promoter group, 9.28%) sells up to 15,00,000 shares.

concentration.note: FY26: Indian Railways alone 40.56% of revenue (46.14% FY25, 56.78% FY24); top 5 customers 85.33%, top 10 92.91%. Government customers account for 53.72% of FY26 revenue (sleeper division 42.61%, MS pipes division 11.11%). Samruddhi Industries, a promoter group entity, is a top-five customer.

litigation_note: Against the company: 1 criminal, 5 tax and 2 civil matters totalling ₹2.82 crore; by the company: 3 criminal and 1 civil totalling ₹5.64 crore. Promoters face 3 criminal, 7 tax, 1 civil and 1 other matter (₹0.34 crore). A CBI FIR (Feb 2025) named the company and a promoter; ₹39 lakh cash was seized, no chargesheet against the company. Contingent liabilities ₹21.87 crore.
strengths: Integrated manufacturing of PSC sleepers and MS pipes, with plants often located at client sites to cut logistics cost.
Order book of ₹682 crore at Mar-26, up from ₹360 crore in Mar-24 (about 37.7% CAGR), giving revenue visibility.
Revenue grew at about 18% CAGR over FY24-26 and PAT rose from ₹3.45 crore to ₹24.98 crore.
EBITDA margin improved from 9.53% to 15.10% and ROCE is 28.02% in FY26.
Long relationship with Indian Railways and reputed private clients such as L&T, KEC and Kalpataru.
Experienced promoters with 25 to 45 years in railway sleeper and infrastructure work.
Debt-equity improved from 2.38x in FY24 to 1.01x in FY26 as net worth grew.
Diversified into MS pipes for pumped storage, precast noise barriers for high-speed rail, and windmill power.

risks.title: Heavy customer concentration
risks.detail: Indian Railways is 40.56% of FY26 revenue; top 5 customers are 85.33% and top 10 are 92.91%. Loss of any large client would hit sales sharply.

risks.title: Dependence on government railway orders
risks.detail: Government sleeper business gave ₹144.21 crore (42.61% of revenue) in FY26 and depends on budgets, tenders and RDSO/Railways approvals; orders are purchase-order based, not long-term contracts.

risks.title: High debt and heavy working capital need
risks.detail: Borrowings were ₹87.42 crore against equity of ₹86.78 crore (1.01x). Cash credit is overdrawn by ₹41.93 crore and ₹75 crore of IPO money goes to working capital.

risks.title: Weak cash conversion
risks.detail: Trade receivables rose from ₹37.18 crore to ₹63.21 crore in two years and inventory is 178 days; operating cash flow fell to ₹27.15 crore in FY26 from ₹38.20 crore, with negative investing and financing flows in some years.

risks.title: Related-party dealings and promoter conflicts
risks.detail: Samruddhi Industries, a promoter group entity, is a top-five customer; the Mohol plant sits on land owned by a promoter without a registered sale deed; promoters have interests in similar businesses; ₹19.73 crore unsecured loans from related parties and others can be recalled.

risks.title: CBI FIR and litigation
risks.detail: A CBI FIR under the Prevention of Corruption Act named the company, a promoter and a director, with ₹39 lakh cash seized; no chargesheet against them. Contingent liabilities are ₹21.87 crore and promoters face several criminal and tax cases.

risks.title: Profit growth tied to services segment and falling bill-to-book
risks.detail: Profit gains came partly from higher-margin services work; bill-to-book ratio fell to 49.35% from 84.07% and the order book may not convert fully to revenue.

risks.title: OFS and use of proceeds
risks.detail: Company gets nothing from the 15,00,000-share OFS by promoter-group entity Vaman Prestressing; the ₹145 crore fresh issue is mainly for working capital and loan repayment, not appraised by any bank.

notes: Standalone Ind AS restated financials, FY26 audited; FY24 is audited special-purpose (Ind AS-adjusted) statements. Source tables in lakhs converted to ₹ crore. Balance sheet columns were garbled and reconstructed (borrowings = non-current + current, matches RHP's ₹8,741.70 lakh). Cash and bank = cash plus other bank balances; cash-credit overdraft is in borrowings. Net worth per RHP KPI table (differs slightly from total equity of ₹86.78 crore); reserves = other equity. Price band, issue size, OFS value, post-issue shares and P/E are blank in the RHP. QIB/anchor/employee reservation percentages not stated; retail at least 70% and NII at least 29%. Current ratio not reported. Peer P/E based on July 23, 2026 prices.
